title: OSHA general industry powered industrial trucks (forklifts) practice questions
description: Free practice questions on OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178 powered industrial trucks. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Which of these vehicles is outside the scope of 29 CFR 1910.178?

options.B: A motorized hand truck
options.D: A fork truck powered by an internal combustion engine

questions.explanation: The section covers fork trucks, platform lift trucks, motorized hand trucks and similar trucks, but it "does not apply to compressed air or nonflammable compressed gas-operated industrial trucks, nor to farm vehicles".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: This section does not apply to compressed air or nonflammable compressed gas-operated industrial trucks, nor to farm vehicles, nor to vehicles intended primarily for earth moving or over-the-road hauling.

questions.question: Under 1910.178, an "approved truck" is listed or approved for fire safety purposes for the intended use by whom?

options.B: The employer's safety committee
options.D: The dealer that sold the truck

questions.explanation: An approved truck is one "listed or approved for fire safety purposes for the intended use by a nationally recognized testing laboratory, using nationally recognized testing standards."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: the term, approved truck or approved industrial truck means a truck that is listed or approved for fire safety purposes for the intended use by a nationally recognized testing laboratory, using nationally recognized testing standards.

questions.question: What does a customer or user need before performing modifications or additions that affect a truck's capacity and safe operation?

options.A: A verbal okay from the truck dealer
options.B: A sign-off from a trained operator
options.C: A note in the daily examination record
options.D: The manufacturer's prior written approval

questions.explanation: Such modifications and additions "shall not be performed by the customer or user without manufacturers prior written approval," and the capacity, operation and maintenance plates, tags or decals "shall be changed accordingly."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Modifications and additions which affect capacity and safe operation shall not be performed by the customer or user without manufacturers prior written approval. Capacity, operation, and maintenance instruction plates, tags, or decals shall be changed accordingly.

questions.question: Additional counterweighting of a fork truck may be done on what condition?

options.A: The load being handled is within rated capacity
options.B: The truck manufacturer approves it
options.C: The truck is used only indoors
options.D: The employer's maintenance supervisor signs off

questions.explanation: "Additional counterweighting of fork trucks shall not be done unless approved by the truck manufacturer."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Additional counterweighting of fork trucks shall not be done unless approved by the truck manufacturer.

questions.question: At a minimum, how often must each powered industrial truck operator's performance be evaluated?

options.B: At least once every three years
options.D: Once every ten years

questions.explanation: An evaluation of each operator's performance "shall be conducted at least once every three years."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An evaluation of each powered industrial truck operator's performance shall be conducted at least once every three years.

questions.question: Which event requires refresher training for a powered industrial truck operator?

options.A: The operator renews a state driver's license
options.B: The employer changes its company name
options.C: The operator completes a year with no accident or near-miss
options.D: The operator is assigned to drive a different type of truck

questions.explanation: Refresher training in relevant topics is required when, among other triggers, "The operator is assigned to drive a different type of truck".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (D) The operator is assigned to drive a different type of truck;

questions.question: Which item must the employer's operator certification include?

options.B: The operator's home address
options.D: The operator's driver's license number

questions.explanation: The certification "shall include the name of the operator, the date of the training, the date of the evaluation, and the identity of the person(s) performing the training or evaluation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The certification shall include the name of the operator, the date of the training, the date of the evaluation, and the identity of the person(s) performing the training or evaluation.

questions.question: Under whose supervision may a trainee operate a powered industrial truck?

options.A: Any coworker who holds a state driver's license
options.B: Another trainee who has finished formal instruction
options.C: The direct supervision of persons with the knowledge, training and experience to train operators and evaluate their competence
options.D: Nobody, once the trainee passes a written test

questions.explanation: Trainees may operate a truck only "Under the direct supervision of persons who have the knowledge, training, and experience to train operators and evaluate their competence" and where the operation "does not endanger the trainee or other employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Trainees may operate a powered industrial truck only: (A) Under the direct supervision of persons who have the knowledge, training, and experience to train operators and evaluate their competence; and (B) Where such operation does not endanger the trainee or other employees.

questions.question: Operator training consists of formal instruction, practical training and what else?

options.A: Evaluation of the operator's performance in the workplace
options.B: A medical examination by a physician
options.C: A written exam graded by OSHA
options.D: A state-issued operator license test

questions.explanation: Training "shall consist of a combination of formal instruction", "practical training" and "evaluation of the operator's performance in the workplace."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Training shall consist of a combination of formal instruction (e.g., lecture, discussion, interactive computer learning, video tape, written material), practical training (demonstrations performed by the trainer and practical exercises performed by the trainee), and evaluation of the operator's performance in the workplace.

questions.question: When charging batteries, how are acid and water combined?

options.B: Acid is poured into water
options.C: Both are poured in at the same time
options.D: Either way, as long as gloves are worn

questions.explanation: "When charging batteries, acid shall be poured into water; water shall not be poured into acid."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When charging batteries, acid shall be poured into water; water shall not be poured into acid.

questions.question: Under 1910.178(p), fuel tanks shall not be filled while what is happening?

options.A: The truck is carrying a load
options.B: The truck is parked outdoors
options.C: The operator is still seated on the truck
options.D: The engine is running

questions.explanation: "Fuel tanks shall not be filled while the engine is running. Spillage shall be avoided."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Fuel tanks shall not be filled while the engine is running. Spillage shall be avoided.

questions.question: While a highway truck is boarded with a powered industrial truck, where are wheel chocks placed?

options.A: Under the front wheels of the powered industrial truck
options.B: Behind the dockboard
options.C: Under the rear wheels of the highway truck
options.D: Nowhere, if the highway truck's engine is off

questions.explanation: "The brakes of highway trucks shall be set and wheel chocks placed under the rear wheels to prevent the trucks from rolling while they are boarded with powered industrial trucks."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The brakes of highway trucks shall be set and wheel chocks placed under the rear wheels to prevent the trucks from rolling while they are boarded with powered industrial trucks.

questions.question: When must the flooring of trucks, trailers and railroad cars be checked for breaks and weakness?

options.B: After the loading is finished
options.D: Only when the trailer is not coupled to a tractor

questions.explanation: The flooring "shall be checked for breaks and weakness before they are driven onto."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The flooring of trucks, trailers, and railroad cars shall be checked for breaks and weakness before they are driven onto.

questions.question: An operator walks 30 feet away from a powered industrial truck, which stays in the operator's view. Under 1910.178(m)(5)(ii), the truck is:

options.A: Attended, because it is still in view
options.B: Attended, as long as the engine is off
options.D: Unattended

questions.explanation: A truck is unattended "when the operator is 25 ft. or more away from the vehicle which remains in his view, or whenever the operator leaves the vehicle and it is not in his view."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A powered industrial truck is unattended when the operator is 25 ft. or more away from the vehicle which remains in his view, or whenever the operator leaves the vehicle and it is not in his view.

questions.question: When must the wheels of an unattended powered industrial truck be blocked?

options.B: When it is parked on an incline
options.D: When it is parked next to another truck

questions.explanation: For an unattended truck, the load engaging means is fully lowered, controls neutralized, power shut off and brakes set, and "Wheels shall be blocked if the truck is parked on an incline."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When a powered industrial truck is left unattended, load engaging means shall be fully lowered, controls shall be neutralized, power shall be shut off, and brakes set. Wheels shall be blocked if the truck is parked on an incline.

questions.question: The operator is dismounted and within 25 ft. of the truck, which is still in view. What does 1910.178(m)(5)(iii) require?

options.A: Nothing, because the truck is attended
options.B: Only that the power be shut off
options.C: Load engaging means fully lowered, controls neutralized and brakes set
options.D: Forks raised to clear the floor and the horn sounded

questions.explanation: In that case "the load engaging means shall be fully lowered, controls neutralized, and the brakes set to prevent movement."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When the operator of an industrial truck is dismounted and within 25 ft. of the truck still in his view, the load engaging means shall be fully lowered, controls neutralized, and the brakes set to prevent movement.

questions.question: Parking a powered industrial truck closer than what distance from the center of railroad tracks is prohibited?

options.B: 3 feet
options.D: 6 feet

questions.explanation: "Parking closer than 8 feet from the center of railroad tracks is prohibited."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Parking closer than 8 feet from the center of railroad tracks is prohibited.

questions.question: When ascending or descending grades in excess of 10 percent, how is a loaded truck driven?

options.B: With the load raised high for better visibility
options.D: With the load upgrade

questions.explanation: "When ascending or descending grades in excess of 10 percent, loaded trucks shall be driven with the load upgrade."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When ascending or descending grades in excess of 10 percent, loaded trucks shall be driven with the load upgrade.

questions.question: Industrial trucks used on a round-the-clock basis must be examined how often?

options.B: After each shift
options.D: Once a month

questions.explanation: Trucks are examined before being placed in service, at least daily, and "Where industrial trucks are used on a round-the-clock basis, they shall be examined after each shift."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Where industrial trucks are used on a round-the-clock basis, they shall be examined after each shift.

questions.question: What must be done before repairs are made to a truck's electrical system?

options.B: The truck is moved into a Class I location
options.D: The fuel tank is filled

questions.explanation: "Trucks in need of repairs to the electrical system shall have the battery disconnected prior to such repairs."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Trucks in need of repairs to the electrical system shall have the battery disconnected prior to such repairs.
